tasks.instructions: In src/agent_arena/control/configuration.py, add a guard at the beginning of validate_origin, before urlsplit(origin). Inspect the original string and raise ValueError when any character is a backslash, satisfies str.isspace(), has a code point below 0x20, or equals 0x7F. Use a concise error explaining that these characters are invalid in an origin. Add a brief comment explaining that validation must precede parsing because parsing can discard some control characters. Keep the existing parsed-origin checks, port validation and return origin.rstrip('/') unchanged. This addresses the malformed inputs reproduced during inspection and the configuration contract in acceptance/proof.py without changing callers or dependencies.

findings: The guard sits before urlsplit(origin) and rejects any character that is a backslash, satisfies str.isspace(), has a code point below 0x20, or equals 0x7F, exactly as specified. It raises ValueError with a concise message and carries the required comment about parsing discarding control characters.
Everything after the guard is unchanged: scheme, hostname, credentials, path, query, fragment, remote-HTTPS and port checks remain, and the function still returns origin.rstrip('/').

The frozen check passed with exit code 0. Because configuration.py no longer matches its baseline hash, acceptance/proof.py exercised the contract: https://example.com and http://127.0.0.1:8790 returned unchanged, and all four malformed inputs (embedded space, backslash, real trailing newline, real leading tab) raised ValueError.

Valid cases not covered by the proof script (https://example.com/, http://localhost:8790/, http://[::1]:8790) contain none of the guarded characters, so they follow the pre-existing code path unchanged.

Scope and constraints hold: only src/agent_arena/control/configuration.py is in the diff, no imports or dependencies were added, acceptance/proof.py is untouched, and the manifest remains at its baseline. The independent review approved with no findings.

Non-blocking: the new guard line is 128 characters, over the 100-character ruff line length configured in pyproject.toml. This is cosmetic, is not enforced by the frozen check, and could be wrapped in a later tidy.
review.summary: The server-address hardening is complete and verified. Addresses containing spaces, tabs, newlines, other control characters or backslashes are now rejected before the URL parser sees them, so the parser can no longer quietly strip those characters and let a bad address through. Normal addresses such as https://example.com, http://127.0.0.1:8790, http://localhost:8790/ and http://[::1]:8790 behave exactly as before, and all the earlier restrictions on scheme, credentials, paths and ports are still in place. The frozen proof check passed and the independent review found no problems. One cosmetic note: the added line is longer than the project's lint limit, which does not affect behavior. This assessment covers only the address-validation half of your request; the phone-recognition change to the app manifest is a separate candidate being assessed on its own. Nothing has been merged: integration into main still waits for your explicit approval at the final gate.

The manifest adds the exact required description and lang value while preserving valid JSON and every existing field. The frozen check and independent review passed. This manifest task meets all acceptance criteria; server-address validation remains a separate task.
